sections.html:
Matthews has 32,769 residents by the July 2025 estimate, up from 29,435 in 2020 and 27,198 in 2010. Mecklenburg County's 2027 revaluation will reset assessments across the town, so timing is part of the decision.

Some owners will want to close before new notices reach mailboxes in early 2027, and others will wait to see them. A listing, a private sale and a cash sale each handle that question differently, so find out how a buyer reads the county's new numbers before you choose.

sections.h2: Matthews home values and household makeup
sections.html:
The midpoint value of an owner-held home is $445,100, and household income runs above $100,000, with a midpoint of $108,611. Owners live in 64.4% of homes. Midpoint gross rent is $1,764, the town counts 11,864 households averaging 2.55 people, and the average commute is 25.2 minutes.

Monthly owner costs are $1,986 for mortgage holders and $591 for those without a loan. About 20.5% of residents are seniors and 21.3% are under 18. People tend to stay, too: 90.0% lived at the same address a year earlier. Those figures point to family buyers who want space and schools, alongside older owners, so accessibility features such as a first-floor bedroom may matter to part of the market.

Many Matthews buyers weigh monthly costs against the price, so keep utility bills, the tax bill and any association fees ready. A buyer who sees $1,986 as a typical mortgage-holder cost will compare that with what your house would take to own. Giving them clear numbers saves time on both sides.

A listing that explains the layout, recent updates and utility costs answers the questions these buyers tend to ask. Check your own house against nearby sales, since a town midpoint says little about one street.

sections.h2: What the 2027 reappraisal means for a sale
sections.html:
Every parcel in Mecklenburg County is revalued to its market value on January 1, 2027, including those in Matthews. The county has kept a four-year schedule since 2019, so this is routine.

The county's initial review of 428,506 parcels showed a median rise of about 15% for residential parcels and 30% for commercial, with more review planned. Owners should expect values and notices in early 2027.

  • Reval.MeckNC.gov lets owners review their property record card and report mistakes, such as an extra bathroom.
  • Elected officials set rates in spring, and bills reach owners in summer.

After a revaluation, rates are normally trimmed to keep revenue level unless elected officials choose otherwise. Until rates are set, any figure for a future bill is only an estimate.

sections.h2: How to question your Matthews assessment
sections.html:
You have two paths: an informal review or a formal appeal heard by the equalization board. The county's tax office page links to an appeal request form.

Deadlines for questioning a value
StepDeadline
Informal reviewWithin 30 days of the notice date
Formal appeal to the equalization boardAsk for a hearing before the board adjourns
Appeal to the Property Tax CommissionWritten notice within 30 days of the mailed ruling, with a copy to the assessor

State law has the board begin meeting between the first Monday of April and the first Monday of May. A lower assessment cuts your carrying cost until you sell.

The town promotes the Mecklenburg County Sportsplex, the Heritage Museum, the Playhouse, a public library and a visitor center, plus events including Summerfest, Beats 'n Bites and Winter Wonderlights.

  • Light rail planning (the Silver Line) and road projects such as John Street and Northeast Parkway improvements appear on the town's pages.
  • Trails include the Four Mile Creek Greenway and the Heritage Trail through historic Crestdale.
  • Town departments handle police, fire and EMS, public works, planning and code enforcement.

The town also lists a bond referendum called Moving Matthews Forward, with parks and transportation bonds, and a proposed one-cent sales tax for transit and roads. Ask the town where each stands before you mention them to a buyer.

sections.h2: Town rules to check before you list
sections.html:
The town's planning pages cover pending zoning and development cases, a Unified Development Ordinance that is being updated, and a code enforcement office. If you plan to add a deck, convert a garage or divide a lot before selling, ask planning staff what approvals apply.

  • Public Works covers garbage, recycling, bulk pickup and yard waste, and the site has a tool for finding your service day.
  • Stormwater and street maintenance fall under Public Works too.
  • The finance pages list the fee schedule, business licenses and tax payment options.

A buyer will want to know what the house sits near, so mention nearby parks, greenways and transit plans accurately, and refer buyers to the town or county for official detail.

sections.h2: What happens at a Matthews closing?
sections.html:
Your deed is filed by the Mecklenburg County Register of Deeds, which collects the seller's excise tax before it records anything. The county bills whoever is the owner of record, so ask the closing office how this year's bill will be divided with the buyer. Back taxes stay with the parcel, and the closing office clears any balance.

A conveyance becomes effective against lien creditors only once registered, which is why the filing matters to buyers. If property tax goes unpaid, the county can bring a foreclosure action that works like a mortgage foreclosure and ends in an auction at the courthouse door. Before the sale is confirmed, the owner can redeem by paying what is owed plus penalties, interest and costs. A payoff letter and a title search ordered before you list will show what is outstanding.

sections.h2: From offer to closing in Matthews
sections.html:
1. Gather the deed, the newest county tax bill and your lender's payoff letter.
  2. Check the property record card and correct errors, like a wrong bathroom count, before buyers notice.
  3. Get offers in writing and ask each buyer how the coming revaluation figures into theirs.
  4. The closing office runs title, writes up the settlement statement and sends the deed to the Register of Deeds.
  5. Review the statement line by line, sign, and receive your proceeds after the payoff and any tax owed.

With no lender involved, a cash buyer closes as fast as the title search allows. If you want to close before new values arrive, say so up front and ask for a closing date in the contract. If you would rather wait for the notice, make sure the buyer understands the price will not change when the county posts a new figure.

Tell every buyer plainly about anything that affects the house, from open permits to a leaking roof. Surprises found at inspection are the most common reason a price drops late in the process, and a cash buyer who has seen the problems up front is less likely to renegotiate.

The routes differ in price, time and effort.

  • An agent can market a well-kept home widely but requires showings and negotiation time.
  • Selling privately avoids the commission but leaves the buyers and paperwork in your hands.
  • Cash buyers accept the house despite its flaws and can close on your calendar, typically at a discount.

If the revaluation affects your timing, compare written offers and ask what each buyer assumes about taxes.

faqs.a: Values are set as of January 1, 2027, and notices are planned for early 2027. The county then repeats the process every four years.

faqs.q: How large are the initial Mecklenburg increases?
faqs.a: The early review showed a median rise near 15% for residential and 30% for commercial parcels. Final values will be posted in 2027.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to request an informal review?
faqs.a: Within 30 days of the date printed on your notice. If you choose a formal appeal instead, it goes before the equalization board.

faqs.q: Who owes the excise tax on a Matthews deed?
faqs.a: The seller. The register of deeds collects it first, then records the deed.

faqs.q: What is a typical Matthews home value?
faqs.a: The midpoint is $445,100 for owned homes. Your house could sit well above or below that, so look at nearby sales and your county record card.
